chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام; and Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubaydillah al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, similarly.
So the proper way regarding these reports is that we interpret them as being upon a kind of taqiyyah, because they agree with the doctrines of some of the 'ammah.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment due to circumstances
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the reports or hadiths under discussion
key_terms.الْوَجْهُ: the proper interpretive approach or method
key_terms.مَذَاهِبِ: legal or doctrinal schools and views

ai.seo_question: Why are some hadith interpreted as having been stated in taqiyyah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This passage gives a juristic method for dealing with certain reports by understanding them as issued in taqiyyah. It states that this is because their apparent content accords with the views held by some among the 'ammah, indicating a need for careful hadith evaluation in legal matters.
